I can refine the description model with a more precise numerical analysis: scores std ~ scale*sqrt(D)=1.1*sqrt(32)≈6.2? Actually z = Kq/sqrt(d), each row dot of 32 iid ~ N(0,1)*1.1 and q: dot std = 1.1*sqrt(32)≈6.22, divided by sqrt(32)→ std ≈1.1*sqrt(32)/sqrt(32)... wait Kq ~ std 1.1*sqrt(32)≈6.2, /sqrt(32)≈1.1. So scores ~ N(0, 1.1²) roughly? No: Kq std = 1.1*sqrt(32) (since q entries unit), divide by sqrt(32)=sqrt(1.1²·32/32)... = 1.1·√32/√32·... hmm: std(Kq)=1.1·√32, /√32 gives std 1.1. So softmax spread ~±2-3 nats; min p ~ e^{-6}/128 ~ 1e-5, far above fp16 subnormal 6e-8, so flush-to-zero unlikely — refine open question. fp16 rounding error per p: ≤2^-11·p; error in y: ||Σ δp v|| ≤ 2^-11·sqrt(Σ v²·...) roughly 2^-11·||v||~2^-11·~11 (V entries ~N(0,1), after centering) → error ~ 2^-11·sqrt(128)·... random-signed δp: std error per row δp~p·2^-12, y error ≈ 2^-12·sqrt(Σp v²)≈2^-12·sqrt(Σp²)·||v||. Not needed to be exact.

Reference norm: ref = p@v_new = p@v - 0.5·(p@v)... p@(v - 0.5(p@v)) = p@v - 0.5(p@v) = 0.5·(p@v). So reference output is exactly 0.5·original output — not near zero, just halved. Original ||p@v|| for 128 tokens of ~N(0,1) values weighted by p (sums to 1): typical ||p@v|| ~ sqrt(Σp²)·1 ≈ for near-uniform p, sqrt(1/128)≈0.09 → ~0.09. Halved ~0.045, well above floor 0.00566. So cancellation is mild (factor 2), not catastrophic. That's a useful analytical refinement to record: c1's premise of near-total cancellation is likely overstated. Record description update.
